mainTopic: Stones near a מרקוליס: the argument between רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן, and whether מרקוליס stones reused for paving roads stay forbidden
overview: The גמרא narrows the argument in the משנה about stones lying near a מרקוליס. Stones close enough that they may have fallen off are forbidden by everyone, and 'beside' in the משנה means within the pile's ארבע אמות, so the argument is about stones farther off but still inside that area. רבי ישמעאל forbids three stones because people sometimes build a small מרקוליס next to a big one. The רבנן disagree, so for them only whether the stones are seen with the pile matters. רבא answers two contradictions: he reads a ברייתא as 'stones that were found' instead of 'that fell', and he separates stones in one area from stones in two areas divided by a raised spot. He also explains that the three-stone shape (one, one, and one on top) is only needed for the main pile. Next comes the story of מרקוליס stones from King ינאי's ruined house that were used to pave roads. רבי יוחנן points to רבי מנחם ברבי סימאי, who walked on those roads. The גמרא then explains the two sides: the strict side treats the stones as an idol's offering, which can never be cancelled, and the lenient side says stones are not like offerings in the בית המקדש. The amud ends as a ברייתא about a גוי who paved roads with such stones begins, and its ruling comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Nearby stones are forbidden by everyone; the argument is about distant stones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that stones close to the מרקוליס, which may have fallen from it, are forbidden according to all opinions. רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן only argue about stones that are farther away.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also with nearby stones, where we can say they fell from the pile, everyone agrees they are forbidden. They only argue about stones that are far away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is narrowing down exactly where the argument in the משנה applies. Close stones are forbidden by everyone, so the argument is only about distant ones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the סוגיא set up that stones that surely fell off are forbidden by everyone. Now it adds one more case to the 'everyone forbids' list: stones close enough that they might have fallen off. That leaves only the far-away stones for the actual argument.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol worshipped by throwing stones onto a pile

phrases.english: Also with nearby stones,
where one can say they fell from it —
everyone agrees they are forbidden.
Where they argue is about distant stones.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּמְקוֹרָבוֹת נָמֵי, דְּאִיכָּא לְמֵימַר מִינֵּיהּ נְפַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier statement in the סוגיא that defined which cases are agreed upon and which are argued about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Nearby stones that may have fallen from the מרקוליס are forbidden by all; the argument is only about distant stones.

steps.title: But the משנה says the stones are right beside the pile
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the last step. The משנה describes the stones as 'beside מרקוליס', which sounds close, not far away.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משנה says 'beside מרקוליס'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects that the משנה's own wording, 'beside', seems to describe stones that are close by.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 said the argument is only about distant stones. But the משנה, where the argument appears, describes the stones as 'beside' the מרקוליס. That sounds like nearby stones, which step 1 said everyone forbids.

phrases.english: But it teaches "beside מרקוליס"!
phrases.notes: This is quoting the wording of our משנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא ״בְּצַד מַרְקוּלִיס״ קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 using the wording of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 1 that the argument is only about distant stones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'beside' in the משנה suggests the disputed stones are close, not far away.

steps.title: 'Beside' means beside its ארבע אמות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'beside' means within the ארבע אמות around the pile. Per רש״י, the close stones that everyone forbids are right next to it, and the distant ones are farther off but still inside the ארבע אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'beside' mean? Beside its ארבע אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: 'beside' means within the ארבע אמות area of the מרקוליס, not right up against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Per רש״י, close stones are about an אמה or half an אמה from the pile, so they might have fallen off it, and everyone forbids them. Distant stones are farther away but still within the ארבע אמות, where they surely did not fall from it. Those ארבע אמות count as 'beside' the pile, so the משנה's argument is about these distant stones. That fits step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: Four amos, the area that counts as belonging to the pile

phrases.english: What is meant by "beside"?
Beside its four amos.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״בְּצַד״? בְּצַד אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a word in the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Beside' meant right next to the pile itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Beside' means next to the pile's ארבע אמות, so the stones are counted as distant.
steps.whatToRemember: Stones right next to the pile are forbidden by everyone. The argument in the משנה is about stones farther off but still within its ארבע אמות (רש״י).

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's reasoning: a small pile may be built next to a big one
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds that idol worshippers sometimes build a small מרקוליס next to a large one. So three stones, which look like a pile, are forbidden, and two stones are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל holds: people make a small מרקוליס beside a big one. Three stones, which look like a מרקוליס, are forbidden. Two are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the reasoning behind רבי ישמעאל's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For these farther-away stones, רבי ישמעאל's worry is not that they fell off the pile. His worry is that three stones together may be a small idol pile of their own. Two stones do not look like a pile, so they are permitted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael holds:
People make a small מרקוליס
beside a large מרקוליס.
Three, which look like a מרקוליס, are forbidden;
two are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל סָבַר: עוֹשִׂין מַרְקוּלִיס קָטָן בְּצַד מַרְקוּלִיס גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defined which stones are argued about, the גמרא now explains each side's reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three distant stones are forbidden because they may be a small idol pile; two are permitted.

steps.title: The רבנן's reasoning: no small pile is built next to a big one
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן hold that people do not build a small מרקוליס next to a large one. So the number of stones does not matter. Only whether they are seen together with the pile decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן hold: people do not make a small מרקוליס beside a big one. Three or two makes no difference. If they are seen with it, they are forbidden. If not, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of the רבנן, the other side of the משנה's argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן do not worry about a separate small pile, counting stones means nothing to them. Their only worry is that the stones fell off the pile. If the stones can be seen together with the pile, that worry applies and they are forbidden.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:
People do not make a small מרקוליס
beside a large מרקוליס.

phrases.aramaic: לָא שְׁנָא שָׁלֹשׁ וְלָא שְׁנָא שְׁתַּיִם,
phrases.english: It makes no difference whether three or two;
those seen with it are forbidden,
those not seen with it are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין עוֹשִׂין מַרְקוּלִיס קָטָן בְּצַד מַרְקוּלִיס גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing reasoning to רבי ישמעאל's view in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Number of stones is irrelevant; stones seen with the pile are forbidden, others permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי ישמעאל worries the stones are a separate small pile, so he counts stones. The רבנן only worry they fell off, so they look at whether the stones are seen with the pile.

steps.title: Quoting the earlier rule: stones known to have fallen are forbidden by all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier statement that when it is known the stones fell from the pile, everyone forbids them. This sets up a contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: where it is known that they fell from it, everyone agrees they are forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is bringing back an earlier statement so that it can question it in the next step. This is a setup line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The statement being quoted says there is no argument at all when we know the stones fell from the pile. The גמרא repeats it word for word because it is about to compare it with a ברייתא that seems to say otherwise.

phrases.english: The Master said:
Where it is known that they fell from it,
everyone agrees they are forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ מִמֶּנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the earlier statement in the סוגיא in order to examine it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stones known to have fallen from the pile are forbidden by all.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows an argument even about stones that fell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא contrasts the quoted rule with a ברייתא. The ברייתא speaks of stones that 'fell' from the מרקוליס and still records an argument between the רבנן and רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Contrast it with this: stones that fell from the מרקוליס. If seen with it, they are forbidden. If not seen with it, they are permitted. רבי ישמעאל says: three are forbidden, two are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction. A ברייתא says there is an argument even when the stones fell from the pile, while the quoted rule says everyone forbids such stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to step 6, stones known to have fallen are forbidden by all, with no exceptions. But in the ברייתא, the רבנן permit fallen stones that are not seen with the pile, and רבי ישמעאל permits two. So the ברייתא seems to have an argument exactly where step 6 said there is none.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast it with (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: And contrast it with this:
Stones that fell from the מרקוליס:
those seen with it are forbidden,
those not seen with it are permitted.
And Rabbi Yishmael says:
Three are forbidden, two are permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּרְמִינְהִי: אֲבָנִים שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ מִן הַמַּרְקוּלִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that stones known to have fallen are forbidden by everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא records an argument, and even some permitted stones, in a case it calls 'fell from the מרקוליס'.

steps.title: רבא: read the ברייתא as 'found', not 'fell'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא should be read as 'stones that were found' near the pile, not 'stones that fell' from it. Then it is not a case where we know they fell.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: don't say 'that fell'. Rather, say 'that were found'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא solves the contradiction by changing one word in the ברייתא: from 'fell' to 'were found'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the ברייתא is about stones that were only found near the pile, we do not know that they came from it. That is a doubtful case, where the argument makes sense. So the rule that stones surely fallen from the pile are forbidden by everyone stays in place.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Do not say "that fell";
rather say "that were found".
phrases.notes: Found near the pile, but we don't actually know they came from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא תֵּימָא ״שֶׁנָּשְׁרוּ״, אֶלָּא אֵימָא ״שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was talking about stones that surely fell off the pile.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about stones merely found near the pile, a doubtful case, so the argument there does not contradict the rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Stones known to have fallen are forbidden by all. The argument between רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן is only about stones found farther away, where we don't know where they came from.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבא is arguing with the ברייתא's ruling. He keeps the ruling and only changes 'fell' to 'found' so the case is a doubtful one.

steps.title: Does רבי ישמעאל really permit two stones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that רבי ישמעאל permits two stones. Another ברייתא quotes him as forbidding two stones near the pile.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי ישמעאל really hold that two stones are permitted? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says two stones in the area of the pile are forbidden, and three stones are forbidden even if they are far away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what we said in Step 4, that רבי ישמעאל permits two stones. It brings a ברייתא where רבי ישמעאל forbids two stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 4 we learned that for רבי ישמעאל, three stones are forbidden and two are permitted. This new ברייתא says two stones are forbidden when they are 'בתפיסה לו', in the pile's area. So the two sources about רבי ישמעאל seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The area that belongs to the pile

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yishmael hold
that two stones are permitted?
phrases.notes: This is רבי ישמעאל's view from Step 4 and from the ברייתא in Step 7.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: Rabbi Yishmael says:
Two stones in its area are forbidden,
three, even if far away, are forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל שְׁתַּיִם מוּתָּרוֹת? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling the contradiction about fallen stones in Step 8, the גמרא now challenges רבי ישמעאל's own position from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim (Step 4) that רבי ישמעאל permits two stones.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא quotes רבי ישמעאל as forbidding two stones in the pile's area, which contradicts the report that he permits two.

steps.title: One area versus two areas
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that two stones are forbidden when they are in the same area as the pile, and permitted when they are in a separate area, divided by a raised spot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is not a problem. Here, the stones are in one area with the pile. There, they are in two areas. What does that look like? When there is a raised spot between them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by saying the two ברייתות talk about different places. When the two stones are in the pile's own area they are forbidden; when they are in a separate area they are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'here' points to the ברייתא that forbids two stones: they are in one area with the pile. The word 'there' points to the ברייתא that permits two stones: they are in a different area. A raised spot between the pile and the stones makes it two separate areas, so the stones clearly did not roll off the pile.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a problem (opens an answer)
Here... there (splits two sources into two different cases)
And what is the case? What does it look like?
A raised spot, a bump in the ground

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי ישמעאל: two stones in the pile's own area are forbidden; two stones in a separate area (with a raised spot in between) are permitted; three stones are forbidden even far away.

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult,
here, it is in one area,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא from Step 9 that forbids two stones.

phrases.english: there, it is in two areas.
And what is the case?
Where there is a raised spot between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לָא קַשְׁיָא, כָּאן בִּתְפִיסָה אַחַת, כָּאן בִּשְׁתֵּי תְּפִיסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (כאן... כאן): each ברייתא speaks about a different location.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות give opposite rulings for the same case of two stones.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two stones in the pile's own area are forbidden; two stones in a separate area, set apart by a raised spot, are permitted.

steps.title: Can stones side by side be a מרקוליס?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether stones simply lying next to each other count as a מרקוליס, since a ברייתא says a מרקוליס has one stone on each side and one on top.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is a מרקוליס made like this? But a ברייתא teaches: These are the stones of a מרקוליס: one on this side, one on that side, and one on top of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that stones lying next to the pile, side by side, could be part of a מרקוליס. A ברייתא describes a מרקוליס as a specific three-stone shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We have been forbidding stones just because they lie near the pile. But the ברייתא says a real מרקוליס is two stones with a third stone set on top. So stones that only sit next to each other should not count as a מרקוליס at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it? Does it count as?

phrases.english: And is a Mercury pile made like this?
phrases.notes: 'Like this' means stones that just lie next to each other on the ground.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
These are the stones of a Mercury place:
one on this side and one on that side,
and one on top of them!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַרְקוּלִיס כְּהַאי גַּוְונָא מִי הָוֵי? וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רבי ישמעאל's view (Steps 4 and 9) that three stones lying together near the pile count as a מרקוליס.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's reasoning (Steps 4 and 9) that three stones lying near the pile look like a מרקוליס of their own and are therefore forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא defines a מרקוליס as two stones with a third on top, so stones just lying next to each other should not count.

steps.title: The three-stone shape is only for the main pile
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the ברייתא describes only the main מרקוליס. Extra stones added to it do not need that shape.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about the main מרקוליס.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge by limiting the ברייתא. It only describes how the main pile is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The core of a מרקוליס is two stones with a third on top. But the stones people add to it afterward do not have to be arranged that way. So stones lying near the main pile can still belong to it.
steps.whatToRemember: The three-stone shape (one, one, and one on top) defines the main מרקוליס. Stones added around it are part of it even without that shape.

phrases.english: Rava said: When that was taught,
it was about the main Mercury pile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כִּי תַּנְיָא הָהִיא בְּעִיקַּר מַרְקוּלִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the ברייתא only speaks about the core of the pile.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every stone of a מרקוליס must be in the three-stone shape.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the main pile needs that shape; added stones do not.

steps.title: The stones from King ינאי's ruined house
steps.stepSummary: Non-Jews set up a מרקוליס in King ינאי's ruined house, and other non-Jews who did not worship it used the stones to pave roads. Some רבנן avoided walking on these roads and some did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: King ינאי's house was destroyed. Non-Jews came and set up a מרקוליס in it. Other non-Jews, who did not worship מרקוליס, came, took the stones, and paved paths and streets with them. Some רבנן kept away from these roads, and some רבנן did not keep away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new story about a real case of מרקוליס stones that were reused for paving roads. It ends by saying the רבנן disagreed, and the גמרא will explain this next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The stones were first set up as a מרקוליס, then taken by people who did not worship it and used for roads. The question is whether the stones are still forbidden, so that one should avoid walking on them. The רבנן split on this, and Steps 17 to 19 explain each side's reason.

phrases.english: The house of King Yannai was destroyed,
non-Jews came and set up a Mercury pile in it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲתוֹ גּוֹיִם אַחֲרִינֵי דְּלָא פָּלְחִי לְמַרְקוּלִיס
phrases.english: other non-Jews who did not worship Mercury came,
took them, and paved paths and streets with them.
There were Rabbis who kept away,
phrases.notes: He means they avoided walking on these paved roads.

phrases.english: and there were Rabbis who did not keep away.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּי יַנַּאי מַלְכָּא חֲרוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: after defining which stones belong to a מרקוליס, the גמרא brings a real-life case of מרקוליס stones that were reused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרקוליס stones were taken by non-worshippers and used for roads, and the רבנן disagreed about whether to avoid walking on them.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: A holy man walks on these roads, so why should we avoid them?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues against avoiding the paved roads, because a very pious person walks on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The son of holy ones walks on them. Should we keep away from them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן weighs in on the argument from Step 13. He says there is no need to avoid the roads, because a famously holy man walks on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof comes from behavior: if someone this careful about עבודה זרה walks on the roads, they must be permitted. The question 'should we keep away?' is a rhetorical way of saying 'we should not.'

keyTerms.meaning: Son of holy ones, a title of honor for a very pious person
We should keep away / hold back

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The son of holy ones walks on them,
phrases.notes: 'Them' means the roads paved with the stones from the מרקוליס, from the story just before this.

phrases.english: and we should keep away from them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּנָן שֶׁל קְדוֹשִׁים מְהַלֵּךְ עֲלֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes a side in the argument among the רבנן from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no need to avoid the roads, because a very pious person walks on them.

steps.title: Who is the 'son of holy ones'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who רבי יוחנן was referring to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is 'the son of holy ones'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: which person did רבי יוחנן mean? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used a title instead of a name, so the גמרא wants to know who it is. This is not an attack. It only asks for identification.

phrases.english: Who is "the son of holy ones"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן נִיהוּ ״בְּנָן שֶׁל קְדוֹשִׁים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the person רבי יוחנן mentioned.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'son of holy ones.'

steps.title: It is רבי מנחם ברבי סימאי, who would not even look at a coin's image
steps.stepSummary: The 'son of holy ones' is רבי מנחם ברבי סימאי. He got the title because he would not even look at the picture on a coin.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי מנחם son of רבי סימאי. Why did they call him 'the son of holy ones'? Because he would not even look at the image on a coin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the person and explains his title. He was so careful to stay away from idol images that he would not even look at the picture on a coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows why his behavior is strong evidence. A man who would not look at a coin's image would surely not walk on stones that were forbidden as עבודה זרה. So if he walked on these roads, they are permitted.

phrases.english: Rabbi Menachem, son of Rabbi Simai.
And why did they call him "the son of holy ones"?
Because he would not even look at the image on a coin.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מְנַחֵם בְּרַבִּי סִימַאי, וְאַמַּאי קָרוּ לֵיהּ ״בְּנָן שֶׁל קְדוֹשִׁים״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the identification question and explains the title.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is רבי מנחם ברבי סימאי, who was so strict that he would not look at the image on a coin.

steps.title: Why did some avoid the roads?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning of the רבנן who kept away from the paved roads.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the one who keeps away from the roads?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to the two groups from Step 13. It asks why the strict group avoided the roads. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The non-Jews who paved the roads did not worship the מרקוליס, so one could think the stones were no longer forbidden. The גמרא wants to know what the strict group based their caution on.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the one who keeps away?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּמַאן דְּפָרֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the two opinions in Step 13 and asks for the reason behind the strict one.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning of the רבנן who avoided the roads.

steps.title: An offering to עבודה זרה can never become permitted
steps.stepSummary: The strict group follows רב, who learns from a פסוק that an offering to עבודה זרה is forbidden forever and cannot be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רב גידל in the name of רב חייא בר יוסף in the name of רב: How do we know that an offering to עבודה זרה can never lose its forbidden status? Because it says: 'They joined themselves to בעל פעור and ate the offerings to the dead.' Just as a dead body stays forbidden forever, an offering to עבודה זרה also stays forbidden forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the strict view. It treats the stones as an offering to the idol, and רב teaches that such an offering can never become permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an idol can lose its forbidden status (ביטול) when a non-Jew cancels it. רב compares an idol's offering to a dead body, which is forbidden forever. So even though non-Jews took the stones for roads, the stones stay forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol
A dead body, which is forbidden to benefit from

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule from רב is a basic principle: an idol can be cancelled, but its offerings never can.

phrases.english: He holds like this,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rav Giddel said that Rav Chiya bar Yosef said that Rav said:
From where do we know that an offering to an idol
can never be cancelled?
As it says: "They joined themselves to Baal Peor,
and ate the offerings to the dead."

phrases.aramaic: מָה מֵת אֵין לוֹ בְּטִילָה לְעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Just as a dead body can never be cancelled,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵין לָהּ בְּטִילָה לְעוֹלָם.
phrases.english: so too an offering to an idol can never be cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כִּי הָא דְּאָמַר רַב גִּידֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the strict view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He treats the stones as an offering to the idol, and such an offering is forbidden forever, like a dead body.

steps.title: Why others did not avoid the roads: stones are not like Temple offerings
steps.stepSummary: The lenient group says something only counts as an idol's offering if it is like what is offered inside the בית המקדש, and stones are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who does not keep away says: I need it to be like what is offered inside, and it is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the lenient view. These stones do not count as an offering, so the rule from Step 18 does not apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree with רב's rule. They only argue about whether these stones count as an 'offering' at all. The lenient side says an offering must be like what is offered in the בית המקדש, and stones are not offered there, so the stones can be cancelled like any idol item.

keyTerms.meaning: Like what is done inside (in the בית המקדש)

steps.confusionAlert: The lenient side does not argue with רב's rule. It only says these stones are not an 'offering', so the rule does not apply to them.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides hold that an idol's offering is forbidden forever. They argue only about whether stones from a מרקוליס count as an offering.

phrases.english: And the one who does not keep away says:
I need it to be like what is offered inside, and it is not.
phrases.notes: 'Inside' means inside the בית המקדש, and stones are never brought there as offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּלָא פָּרֵישׁ, אָמַר: בָּעֵינָא כְּעֵין פְּנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reason, in contrast to Step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An idol's offering must resemble an offering in the בית המקדש. Stones do not, so they are not a forbidden offering.

steps.title: A ברייתא brought by רבה בר ירמיה about a גוי who paved roads with מרקוליס stones
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף בר אבא reports that רבה בר ירמיה brought a ברייתא about a גוי who paved roads and theaters with stones from a מרקוליס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף בר אבא said: רבה בר ירמיה came to our place, and he brought a ברייתא with him: A גוי who took stones from a מרקוליס and paved roads and theaters with them...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new source that deals with exactly this kind of case. This is a setup line. The ruling of the ברייתא comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the question of the paved roads was settled by reasoning and by people's behavior. Now a ברייתא appears that speaks directly about a גוי paving roads with מרקוליס stones. Its ruling will shed light on the argument above.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching from the time of the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Abba said:
Rabba bar Yirmeya happened to come to our place,
and when he came he brought a ברייתא with him:
A non-Jew who brought stones from a מרקוליס
and paved roads and theaters with them —

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר אַבָּא: אִיקְּלַע רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה לְאַתְרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that deals directly with the case of paved roads discussed above.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces a ברייתא about a גוי who paved roads with מרקוליס stones. Its ruling continues on the next amud.
